text: Henry Nolan’s motive to evoke nostalgia and a sense of belonging is structurally reinforced through his use of the old mill as a central metaphor. By positioning the mill as a symbol of stability and resistance against modernity, Nolan aligns the thematic structure of the text with his intent to highlight the importance of tradition and community. This metaphorical framework allows the collection of short stories to function not just as narratives, but as a cohesive argument for preserving the past in a rapidly changing world, thereby linking the author’s emotional goal directly to the symbolic architecture of the work.
